Gīta-govinda
(‘song concerning Govinda [or कृष्ण]’)
------------------------------------------
One of the most popular of all the lyrics in Sanskrit is the Gītagovinda of जयदेव (12th cent. A. D.). The work comprises 12 sargas or sections, each containing 24 stanzas set to मुसिच्. The poet himself has fixed the rāgas (tunes) and tālas (time-beats) so that they can be sung by musicians and also adopted by dancers.
The main theme is the love of राधा for कृष्ण and his response.
The work is considered as a master-piece in Sanskrit poetry and a model for many a later writer. Perfection of metrical form and a wonderful display of human feelings and sentiments mark it out as an extraordinary piece of Sanskrit literature. It also shows to what heights the सन्स्क्रित् लन्गुअगे can rise as regards beauty, elegance and even sublimity.
See also JAYADEVA.

Gītārthasaṅgraha
(‘an abridgement of the essentials of the ’)
------------------------------------------
Though the Viśiṣṭādvaita Vedānta philosophy has been expounded and elaborated by Rāmānuja (A. D. 1017-1137), the contribution of his predecessors was considerable. Among them यामुनाचार्य (A. D. 918-1038) was the most celebrated. He wrote three works in Sanskrit, out of which the Gītārthasaṅgraha is also one. On this, two commentaries are available: Gītārthasaṅgraha-rakṣā by वेदान्त देशिक (A. D. 1268-1370) and Gītārtha-saṅgraha-dīpikā by Varavara मुनि (A. D. 1370-1443).
The work has only 32 ślokas or verses summarising the whole Bhagavadgītā.
The first verse declares that God, the Supreme, is नारायण and that he can be attained by भक्ति or devotion alone.
Verses 3 to 5 state that the Gītā can be divided into three ṣaṭkas or triads of 6 chapters each. The first ṣaṭka (chs. 1-6) states that ātmānubhūti or self-realisation can come through the performance of desireless action (niṣkāma कर्म), know-ledge (jñāna) and meditation (yoga).
The second ṣaṭka states that भक्ति-योग, which results from कर्मयोग and ज्ञानयोग, is the means for realising God and gives some details about it.
The third ṣaṭka deals with the rest of the relevant topics (which subserve the previous two ṣaṭkas), gives some details of प्रधान or प्रकृति (matter), पुरुष (the individual self), ईश्वर (God) and some disciplines relating to ज्ञान (knowledge), भक्ति (devotion) and कर्म (work).
The verses 5 to 22 give very briefly, the gist of the eighteen chapters of the Gītā, chapter by chapter.
The ideas spread over the rest of the ten verses—23 to 32—may be summarised as follows:
Karmayoga is performing austerity (tapas), undertaking pilgrimages (tīrtha-yātrā), doing sacrifices and other similar activities.
Bhaktiyoga is meditation on God with love.
Obligatory (nityakarma) and occasio-nal (naimittika-कर्म) works are associated with all the yogas.
Removal of nescience (ajñāna) leads to the realisation of the Self (the आत्मन्) whereas practising supreme devotion (parābhakti) towards God will help the aspirant to attain the world of God.
Bhaktiyoga can give the aspirant whatever he wants—prosperity here or salvation (kaivalya).
The man of supreme knowledge is also a man of supreme devotion since they coalesce in the final stage.
The perfect being finds his supreme satisfaction in several acts connected with devotion to God such as meditation, speaking about him, bowing down to him, singing his praises and so on. In fact all his activities are directed only to please God under all circumstances.
See also BHAGAVADGĪTĀ and YĀMUNĀ-CĀRYA.

Gītā Press
------------------------------------------
Generally speaking, हिन्दुइस्म् and organised propagation of its tenets are poles apart! The very nature of हिन्दुइस्म्, which lays great stress on personal मुक्ति or individual लिबेरतिओन्, prevents it.
गोरख्पुर्">Gītā Press at GorakhpurHowever, over the last two centuries, several attempts have been made to propagate either general हिन्दुइस्म् or some of its cults through various religious movements and organisations. One such organisation that is rendering great service to the cause of हिन्दुइस्म् quietly and unostentatiously, is the Gita Press of गोरख्पुर् in Uttar Pradesh.
Since the Bhagavadgītā or the Gītā is the most popular scripture, accepted by almost all the sections of the Hindus, the late Jaydayāl Goeṅkā established the गीता प्रेस्स् in A. D. 1923. Its Govind Bhavan Kāryālaya (office) at Calcutta has been registered under the Registration of Societies Act of West Bengal, 1961. The institution is managed by a board of trustees.
The primary purpose of establishing the गीता प्रेस्स् was to propagate हिन्दुइस्म् by printing and selling at a highly subsidised price, Hindu religious literature. This includes the Bhagavadgītā, the उपनिषद्स्, the Rāmāyaṇa, the Mahā-bhārata, the Bhāgavata, the पुराणस्, other religious works like the Rāmcarit-Mānas, the Nārada Bhaktisūtras, Vedāntic works like the Vivekacūḍāmaṇi, compendiums of stotras or hymns, lives of saints and so on.
Till now (March 1998) a total number of 270 million copies of these books have been printed and circulated.
These books have been mostly in Sanskrit and Hindi languages as also English. Recently, the same books are being brought out in other regional languages also.
Two monthly journals—Kalyāṇ in Hindi and Kalyāṇa Kalpataru in English—are also being published. These journals have become extremely popular.
The main gate of the गीता प्रेस्स् of गोरख्पुर् is very impressive and has incorporated in itself the special architectural features from several parts of India.
The Līlā Citra Mandir houses hundreds of pictures depicting the incidents from the lives of राम and कृष्ण. Ślokas from the Gītā and the sayings of saints like Tulasīdās, कबीर्, Dādūdayāl, Sundardās, Rahīm and others have been inscribed on the walls. Every year, during the गीता Jayanti celebrations, special exhibitions of Gītā literature (including rare books in several languages) are organised.
There is a गीता Bhavan at Svargāśram (Uttar Pradesh) on the bank of the river गङ्गा, run by the गीता प्रेस्स्. It has more than 1000 rooms, to accommodate sādhakas (spiritual aspirants) who throng to the place now and then.
The गीता प्रेस्स् is also running a Ṛṣikul-Brahmacaryāśrama at Cūrū in Rajasthan, to impart training on the गुरुकुल model, to willing students.
The Govind Bhavan Kāryālaya at Calcutta, the Head Quarters of the organisation has facilities for the chanting of the Gītā and religious discourses. An āyurvedic dispensary is also attached to the same.
